name: Respect
definition: We respect others, make every effort to understand each other, take responsibility and do our best to build mutual trust.

rows.situation: When you disagree with someone's call
rows.under: Writes them off. Their reasons are not worth hearing.
rows.justRight: Works to understand why they see it that way, then takes a position.
rows.over: Spends so long understanding that you never take a position.

rows.situation: When the work has hurt someone
rows.under: Explains why it was reasonable from your side.
rows.justRight: Takes responsibility, and does the work of repairing the trust.
rows.over: Apologizes so thoroughly that the repair never starts.

rows.situation: When trust is not yet there
rows.under: Proceeds as if it were, and is surprised when it breaks.
rows.justRight: Does what you said you would, in the small things, until trust is real.
rows.over: Demands trust as a precondition, before you have given any.

rows.situation: When a stakeholder is not in the room
rows.under: Talks as if they do not exist. Their interest is an inconvenience.
rows.justRight: Represents them fairly, including the parts that complicate the plan.
rows.over: Blocks every move on their behalf without checking whether they would have cared.

rows.situation: When respect is confused with agreement
rows.under: Calls disagreement disrespect, and people stop saying what they see.
rows.justRight: Disagrees without diminishing the person. Understanding is not the same as agreeing.
rows.over: Softens every disagreement into a compliment, and the real issue never gets named.

rows.situation: When the other person's context is unfamiliar
rows.under: Judges from your own context and calls it a standard.
rows.justRight: Puts in the work to learn theirs, then holds a shared standard.
rows.over: Treats every difference as equally valid, including the ones that break the work.
